messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

output:
This year, the team shipped fewer things at once and finished more of them. The checkout redesign moved from three competing prototypes to one, launched in October, and cut cart abandonment by eleven percent. The migration off the old queue system took longer than planned, but it removed the class of timeout bugs that used to eat a Friday every month.

We split the platform team from the product teams in March. That gave product engineers a clearer path to ship without waiting on shared infrastructure, and gave the platform team room to fix the deploy pipeline properly instead of patching it between requests. Deploy time dropped from twenty-two minutes to six.

Incidents were down: four this year against eleven last year. Two of those four came from the same root cause, a config drift issue in staging, which we closed with a validation step in the CI pipeline.

Hiring was slower than we wanted. We brought on three engineers instead of the six we planned, and leaned on contractors to cover the gap on the mobile rewrite. That rewrite is about sixty percent done and will carry into next year.

The postmortem process changed too: we moved from a shared doc to a short recorded walkthrough, and attendance at the follow-up review went up because people could watch it on their own time.

Next year the priority is finishing the mobile rewrite and paying down the test coverage gap in the billing service, which is still under forty percent.
